title: Synthesis, crystal structure and magnetic properties of μ4-oxo-centered tetranuclear lanthanide clusters

synthesis.procedure: Shared preparation of 1 and 2: 1,3-bis(2-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzylamino)propan-2-ol (H3L, 0.1 mmol) and Ln(NO3)3·5H2O (0.2 mmol; Ln = Gd for 1) in methanol (10 ml) were stirred at room temperature for 5 days. A white precipitate was collected and washed with methanol. The oxo ligand is attributed to residual water; yield of 1 and 2 decreased dramatically in carefully pre-dried MeOH, and Karl–Fischer titration indicated ~0.5% water in MeOH as optimal.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: White precipitate collected and washed with methanol.

properties.summary: Solid-state magnetism of 1 at 100 Oe (2–300 K) follows Curie–Weiss behaviour with θ = −2.18 K. Room-temperature μeff per molecule is 15.3 μB (close to 15.9 μB for four non-interacting Gd3+), nearly constant to ca. 50 K, then drops to 9.48 μB at 2 K, attributed mainly to weak intra- and intermolecular antiferromagnetic Gd–Gd coupling.

measurements.conditions: χM−1 vs T Curie–Weiss fit; 100 Oe; 2–300 K; diamagnetic correction

synthesis.procedure: Shared preparation of 1 and 2: 1,3-bis(2-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzylamino)propan-2-ol (H3L, 0.1 mmol) and Ln(NO3)3·5H2O (0.2 mmol; Ln = Tb for 2) in methanol (10 ml) were stirred at room temperature for 5 days. A white precipitate was collected and washed with methanol. Colourless single crystals of 2 were obtained by slow evaporation of the methanol solution at room temperature for a few days. Residual water in MeOH (~0.5% by Karl–Fischer titration) is required for good yield of the μ4-oxo cluster.
synthesis.time: 5 days stirring; crystals after a few days of evaporation
synthesis.vessel_or_method: stirring in methanol; crystallization by slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: White precipitate collected and washed with methanol. Colourless single crystals of 2 from slow evaporation of methanol at room temperature for a few days.

properties.summary: Solid-state magnetism of 2 at 100 Oe (2–300 K) follows Curie–Weiss behaviour with θ = −5.22 K (OCR of the second Weiss constant is imperfect). Room-temperature μeff per molecule is 15.0 μB, well below 19.4 μB expected for four free Tb3+ ions, suggesting antiferromagnetic coupling. μeff decreases continuously on cooling and drops abruptly below 75 K to 11.2 μB at 2 K, ascribed mainly to ligand-field splitting of Tb3+ with a possible antiferromagnetic contribution.
